title: Correct magnetic field magnitude (1)
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (1) must be numerically equivalent to B = (2√3)/3 T or approximately 1.155 T.

title: Correct minimum magnitude (2)
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (2) must be B_min = 1 T.

title: Correct field direction (2)
description: Essential: The student must state the direction of the magnetic field in part (2) as along the suspension line (or equivalent) and downward.

title: Force equilibrium for part (1)
description: Important: The solution must resolve forces horizontally and vertically, applying equilibrium to relate magnetic force to weight via tan(30°).

title: Ampere's law application
description: Important: The student must correctly apply the formula F = BIL to relate magnetic force, field, current, and length for both parts.

title: Force triangle for minimum B
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must construct a force triangle/vector diagram and identify that the minimum magnetic force is mg sin(30°).

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The working should demonstrate consistent use of SI units (kg, m, s, A, T) without conversion errors.

title: Sign/direction error in force
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly assigns the direction of the magnetic force (e.g., using wrong hand rule) leading to an incorrect field direction.

title: Trigonometric error
description: Pitfall: Penalize a clear misuse of sine/cosine/tangent in the force balance (e.g., using sin(30°) instead of tan(30°) for part (1)).
